shapes.quote: The difference with presentations is that you are expected to communicate your ideas orally, in front of audience, and you might also be expected to create visual aids, like a PowerPoint slideshow, to complement spoken content.
It is therefore by creating a well-researched and confidently delivered presentation that you can exercise greater ownership of your understanding and disciplinary knowledge.

cards.baseContent: A short follow-on from the generic concept-definition, showing the concept in the learner's own subject; the context pack supplies the whole prose.

cards.tierBrief: An application task: the learner uses the concept on a realistic case; distractors are near-misses, not obvious errors.
cards.baseContent: The lesson's interactive concept activity: the task itself teaches the concept (learn by doing), authored generically.

cards.tierBrief: A multi-step contrast across a realistic task; the stronger version shows judgement, not just more effort.

cards.tierBrief: Guidance for applying the practice across modules and heavier tasks; some self-management expected.

cards.tierBrief: Test application of the concept to a typical task in the subject; distractors are partial or misapplied versions, not obvious errors.

shapes.quote: The first and most important is 'less is more'.
Visual aids are an integral element of presentations; but they support rather than replace the spoken part.

lessons.title: Planning, structuring, and designing your presentation

grounding.heading: Planning, structuring, and designing your presentation

shapes.quote: Natalie's poor performance highlights the different steps you need to take if you're going to create an effective presentation.

The first point to acknowledge about Natalie's experience is that many of you will find public speaking and delivering presentations nerve-wracking, particularly when the audience is made up of what Natalie calls 'important people'.

In short, presentations, when used in a selection process, function as a statement of your graduate identity.

shapes.quote: Group work, like presentations, is very closely linked to your graduate identity because it requires behaviours and competencies required in the workplace.

For tutors, the value of group work lies in the processes behind the creation of that product rather than the product itself, but for students who are focused on marks and performance, this can be difficult to understand.
